rounds.proof_sketch: Mutation is in the template specialization `softsign_kernel<half>` (line 24: `idx < size - 1`). With input dtype=torch.float32, AT_DISPATCH_FLOATING_TYPES_AND_HALF dispatches to the generic `softsign_kernel<float>` template, which retains the original unmutated condition `idx < size`. The half specialization is only invoked for torch.float16 inputs. Since dtype is fixed to float32, the mutated code path is never executed.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation modifies the boundary condition in the half-precision (float16) template specialization of the CUDA kernel. The CUDA code uses AT_DISPATCH_FLOATING_TYPES_AND_HALF which dispatches to different kernel instantiations based on input dtype: float inputs use the generic template, half inputs use the specialized template. Since the input specification fixes dtype to torch.float32, the dispatch always selects the generic template<float> instantiation, which contains the original unmutated condition 'if (idx < size)'. The mutated condition 'if (idx < size - 1)' in the half specialization is never executed regardless of what numerical values are placed in the float32 tensor.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under the fixed contract. To expose the mutation, one would need to use torch.float16 (half precision) input, which would cause the last element (index size-1 = 262143) to be skipped. However, the input specification constrains dtype to torch.float32, making the mutated half-precision code path unreachable through value-level changes alone.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing for CUDA kernels with type-dispatching (AT_DISPATCH_*) should systematically test all supported dtypes (float16, float32, float64) to ensure full code path coverage. Consider adding dtype as a test dimension in the testing contract, or create separate test specifications for each supported dtype to catch mutations in type-specialized code paths.
